title: Check yourself: limits of string literals

questions.stem: A support tool runs `st.executeUpdate("UPDATE accounts SET locked = TRUE " + "-- abusers only " + "WHERE failed_logins > 5")` on a table of 40 accounts, 3 of which have more than five failed logins. What happens?

options.text: All 40 accounts are locked, since the statement is one line and the comment runs on to its end
options.says: the pieces are joined with no line break between them, so the -- comment takes in the WHERE clause, and an UPDATE without a condition changes every row

options.text: All 40 accounts are locked, since each piece joined by + reaches the database as a statement of its own
options.says: the + of literals produces one string, a single statement; the database never sees the pieces

options.text: The 3 accounts are locked, since each piece joined by + starts on a line of its own in the value
options.says: the line breaks in the source are outside the quotes, so the value holds none

options.text: The 3 accounts are locked, since the comment ends where the literal that holds it ends
options.says: the literals are joined into one string before the database sees it, so the comment ends only at a line break or the end of the statement

origin.section: A Value Split Across Lines Has a Seam at Every `+`, and a Missing `\n` or Space There Changes It

questions.stem: A repository method returns a twelve-line query written as twelve string literals joined with +, with no variables in it. In review, a colleague asks for a StringBuilder instead, to save eleven concatenations on each call. What do you answer?

options.text: Keep the +, since the JIT merges the twelve constant pieces into one builder once the method is hot
options.says: there is nothing left to merge at run time: an expression of constants is folded by javac

options.text: Keep the +, since javac has already joined the twelve pieces into one string in the class file
options.says: a constant expression is folded at compile time (javap shows a single ldc), so each call loads one existing string

options.text: Use the builder, since each + between two literals creates a new String every time the line runs
options.says: the literals are folded at compile time, so the line creates no String at run time

options.text: Use the builder, since the + expression compiles to one invokedynamic concatenation that runs on each call
options.says: an expression made only of literals is folded by javac into one constant (javap shows a single ldc), so no concatenation runs on any call

origin.section: A Value Split Across Lines Has a Seam at Every `+`, and a Missing `\n` or Space There Changes It

questions.stem: A stock report appends `String.format("%s;%d%n", sku, qty)` for each row. Its unit test compares the report for two rows with `"K-88;4\nP-03;1\n"` and passes on the Linux build server. A colleague runs the same test on Windows. What happens?

options.text: It fails, since the expected string's \n is compiled to the line ending of the machine that ran javac
options.says: \n is U+000A in the class file whatever machine compiled or runs it

options.text: It fails, since %n is turned into the line ending of the machine whose JVM runs the format
options.says: %n writes the line.separator property, CR LF on Windows, while the expected \n stays a single line feed

options.text: It passes, since %n and \n both become the line ending of the machine whose JVM runs the code
options.says: only %n follows the platform; \n is fixed at compile time

options.text: It passes, since %n and \n are both a single line feed until the text is written to a file
options.says: String.format applies line.separator when it formats; the string itself already holds CR LF on Windows

origin.section: `\n` Is Always a Line Feed; `%n`, `println` and `lineSeparator()` Follow the Platform

questions.stem: To get rid of the escaped quotes, a team moves a shipping e-mail into a text block whose second line reads `Hi ${firstName}, order #{orderId} is on its way.` The method has local variables firstName and orderId and returns the text block as it is, compiled with javac 21 and no extra flags. What does the customer read?

options.text: Their own name and order number, since javac replaces each placeholder with the variable of that name
options.says: a text block has no interpolation; ${firstName} is plain text in the value

options.text: Their own name and order number, since the JVM fills each placeholder from the method's variables
options.says: nothing fills placeholders at run time either; values go in through formatted, + or bind parameters

options.text: The placeholders as typed, since a text block is raw: it keeps every character exactly as written
options.says: a text block does process escapes, as a traditional literal does; it is not raw, it only has no interpolation

options.text: The placeholders as typed, since a text block fills in nothing: a name in it is just characters
options.says: a text block has no interpolation: ${...} and #{...} are ordinary characters, and values go in through formatted, + or bind parameters

origin.section: A Text Block Removes the Escaped Quotes and the Seams, Not the Backslashes or the Values
